name: Crazy Rummy
description: Crazy Rummy is a multi-deal rummy game in which the wild rank changes each deal (Aces wild in deal 1, Twos wild in deal 2, and so on). Players draw, meld, lay off, and discard to go out with the lowest cumulative score over the series.

overview.description: Crazy Rummy is a multi-deal rummy game in which the wild rank changes each deal (Aces wild in deal 1, Twos wild in deal 2, and so on). Players draw, meld, lay off, and discard to go out with the lowest cumulative score over the series.

history.origins: Crazy Rummy is documented as a North American rummy family game with many local names and house-rule branches; it is also played in the UK (e.g. South Wales and Dorset).
timeline: 20th century: Circulates as a 13-deal rotating-wild-card rummy game.
Modern era: Documented with named variants such as Biddies, Beanie, Benny, and Ace to Ace.
history.cultural: Often played as a social score-accumulation game where lowest total score after the full sequence wins.
history.evolution: Core structure remains a rotating wild-rank, 13-deal progression; local variants change deck count, card values, and detailed meld rules.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck, usually without jokers in base rules.
setup.dealing: Deal 7 cards to each player and an eighth card to player left of dealer, who begins.
setup.equipment: Deck, score sheet, and chips or tokens if side payments are used.

rules.objective: Finish each deal by going out (melding all cards and discarding one), and end the full series with the lowest cumulative penalty score.
rules.gameplay: A game is played over sequential deals with changing wild rank. On each turn, player draws from stock or top discard, may meld/lay off/replace wilds if allowed, then discards one card. When a player goes out, others score cards left in hand. Continue through the planned deal sequence.
keyRules: Wild rank changes by deal (Ace, 2, 3 ... King in the 13-deal form).
Valid melds are sets and runs; wild cards can substitute as allowed by house rules.
A player may lay off onto existing melds after their first meld.
To go out, player must usually discard a final card.
Scoring is cumulative and low score wins the full game.

strategy.basic: Meld early to reduce penalty risk while keeping flexibility for final discard.
strategy.intermediate: Track current wild rank and reserve natural cards that can reclaim wild substitutions in table melds.
strategy.advanced: Balance immediate layoff value against holding structure for a faster go-out line in the current wild-rank environment.
tips: Prioritize reducing high-value deadwood before late-turn risk windows.
Plan around wild-card transitions between deals when managing cumulative score.

variations.name: 13-Deal Standard
variations.description: Classic sequence from Aces wild through Kings wild over 13 deals.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: 13-Deal Standard is the base game; no engine overrides needed.

scoring.description: After each deal, players score points for unmelded cards in hand; cumulative low score wins after full deal sequence.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest cumulative score after the planned number of deals.

synthesis.shortDescription: A multi-deal rummy in which the wild rank rotates each deal and lowest cumulative penalty score wins.
